key_insight: The paper introduces ConfSeq, a conformation description language that lets language models understand and generate 3D molecular structures. This bridges text-based AI with molecular geometry, enabling strong performance on conformer prediction, 3D molecule generation, and molecular representation.
problem_solved: Many AI models struggle to work directly with three-dimensional molecular structures because standard language formats do not naturally encode molecular conformations. This work addresses the challenge of representing and predicting 3D molecular geometry in a way that language models can learn effectively.
method: Defines ConfSeq, a language for describing molecular conformations in a machine-readable sequence format.
Uses this representation to adapt language models for 3D molecular tasks such as conformer prediction and molecule generation.
Demonstrates that the approach supports both structural understanding and generative modeling of molecules with strong performance.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ConfSeq provides a practical bridge between foundation models and molecular modeling tasks that depend on 3D structure. It could simplify building models for chemistry, drug discovery, and materials design by making molecular geometry more compatible with modern language-model workflows.
